lines.text: Brasher's gold doubloon flipped America's motto.
Ephraim Brasher was a goldsmith and jeweler in New York.
lines.say: Ee fray im Brasher was a goldsmith and jeweler in New York.

lines.text: People brought him foreign gold coins to weigh.
His EB stamp counted as proof of weight and purity.
In 1787, he asked New York for a copper coin contract.
lines.say: In seventeen eighty seven, he asked New York for a copper coin contract.

lines.text: The state refused, and he struck gold doubloons that year.
One side shows New York's coat of arms and his name.
The other shows an eagle and the motto Unum E Pluribus.
Those are the words of E pluribus unum in a new order.
Only seven of these doubloons are known.
lines.say: Only seven of these doubloons are known.

post.caption: Brasher's gold doubloon flipped America's motto. Ephraim Brasher was a goldsmith and jeweler in New York, and people brought him foreign gold coins to weigh. In 1787, he asked New York for a copper coin contract. The state refused, and he struck gold doubloons that year. One side shows New York's coat of arms and his name. The other shows an eagle and the motto Unum E Pluribus, the words of E pluribus unum in a new order. Only seven of these doubloons are known.
